# Governance Without TERM Token Veto Configuration Proof

## 1. High Level Conclusion

```
Branch 1 (the slow path, for real proposals)
  ProposerSafe (5/11) ------module------> Delay Modifier ------module------> OwnerlessSafe (9/9) ------DEVOPS_ROLE------> Term Protocol
  (+ ConfigLockGuard)                     (+ PauseGuard)                  (+ ConfigLockGuard)

Direct path (all nine OwnerlessSafe signers together: no delay, veto or pause)
  OwnerlessSafe (9/9) ------DEVOPS_ROLE------> Term Protocol

Branch 2 (the DelayOwnerSafe's veto path, whose only power is to veto)
  DelayOwnerSafe (5/11) ------owner------> Delay Modifier
  (+ ConfigLockGuard)

Pause controls
  PauseSafe (2/9) --pause-->               PauseGuard
  ProposerSafe   --unpause / setPauser-->  PauseGuard
```

**Trust assumption:** Despite its name, the OwnerlessSafe has nine Term multisig holders as owners and a threshold of 9, high enough that its direct path has more friction than going through the Delay Modifier.

The conclusions drawn from these proofs establish the following propositions:

1. The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe and the Term multisig holders on the OwnerlessSafe, and only they, may execute DEVOPS_ROLE methods, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, and guard constant for the ProposerSafe and OwnerlessSafe; 2. the module guard constant for the OwnerlessSafe; 3. the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown, and txExpiration constant for the Delay Modifier; and 4. the pauser and admin constant for the PauseGuard, provided DEVOPS_ROLE method calls from the ProposerSafe are not vetoed, and are executed while the PauseGuard is not paused and before the 24-hour expiration period following the cooldown ends.

2. Only the Term multisig holders on the DelayOwnerSafe may veto Delay Modifier transactions within the 24-hour veto window, in which a Delay Modifier transaction cannot be executed until txCooldown has passed since it was queued, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard constant for the DelayOwnerSafe, and 2. the owner, target, modules, guard constant for the Delay Modifier, and 3. the txCooldown constant for the Delay Modifier.

3. Only the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe may pause, and only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe may unpause, the execution of Delay Modifier transactions, and if a pause outlasts the 24-hour expiration period following the cooldown, the Delay Modifier transaction can only be skipped or vetoed, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard constant for the PauseSafe and ProposerSafe, and 2. the guard, txCooldown, txExpiration constant for the Delay Modifier, and 3. the pauser and admin constant for the PauseGuard.

4. The owners for the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, and DelayOwnerSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, or DelayOwnerSafe. The fallbackHandler, modules, guard, module guard for the OwnerlessSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The following: 1. the fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the ProposerSafe and DelayOwnerSafe, and 2. the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown, txExpiration for the Delay Modifier cannot be changed by anyone.

5. The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe. The pauser for the PauseGuard can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by anyone.

Only Term multisig holders can execute DEVOPS_ROLE methods, and this cannot be changed other than through Term multisig approval.

## 2. Evidence Classification

This document uses two classes of evidence to establish the security and functional properties of the governance configuration:

- **Formal Verification (FV) evidence** establishes that, assuming the stated configuration, the relevant contracts enforce the claimed security and functional properties. These properties are proved with the Certora Prover, a formal verification tool. For the guards (PauseGuard and ConfigLockGuard), the proofs run on the contract code that was deployed, the code at tag [`2.1.0`](https://github.com/term-finance/zodiac-modifier-roles-v1/tree/2.1.0). The proofs cover privileged entry points, authorized callers, configuration immutability, the absence of alternative execution paths, and the intended functionality. In the tables below, FV evidence is labeled **FV —** and names each Certora rule; ✅ marks a rule that passes.
- **Deployment evidence** states the configuration the 2.1.0 deployment must have for the formal verification evidence to apply: owners, modules, guards, thresholds, roles, and other relevant state. 2.1.0 is a proposal, not a live deployment, so none of it has been read on chain yet. In the tables below, deployment evidence is labeled **On-chain —**; ⏳ marks a requirement to verify against on-chain state, at a stated block, once the 2.1.0 contracts are deployed.

These two classes of evidence are complementary. Formal verification evidence does not by itself establish that the deployed contracts have the configuration being proved, and deployment evidence does not by itself establish that the deployed configuration enforces the claimed security and functional properties.

**Safe versions.** The ProposerSafes and OwnerlessSafes already deployed run GnosisSafeL2 v1.3.0 or SafeL2 v1.4.1, and any deployed from now on will run SafeL2 v1.5.0. No DelayOwnerSafe or PauseSafe exists yet, so each will be deployed on SafeL2 v1.5.0. The formal verification evidence therefore covers the ProposerSafe and OwnerlessSafe on GnosisSafeL2 v1.3.0, SafeL2 v1.4.1 and SafeL2 v1.5.0, and the DelayOwnerSafe and PauseSafe on SafeL2 v1.5.0 only. Each version is the L2 build of the Safe, so the rules run against that build.

Configuration items marked ⏳ (pending deployment) describe the configuration of the proposed 2.1.0 deployment and are not established yet. Each must be verified against on-chain state once the 2.1.0 contracts are deployed.

| P2.8  | The Term multisig holders on the DelayOwnerSafe may veto Delay Modifier transactions within the 24-hour veto window, in which a Delay Modifier transaction cannot be executed until txCooldown has passed since it was queued.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **FV — A Delay Modifier transaction cannot be executed until txCooldown has passed since it was queued:**<br>• DP-31 `onlyExecuteNextTxReachesTheTarget` ✅ passes: over every write function of the Delay Modifier and the PauseGuard, only `executeNextTx` hands a transaction to the Delay Modifier's target. So `executeNextTx` is the only way a queued transaction is executed.<br>• DP-25 `executeNextTxConsumesOnlyTheEntryAtTxNonce` ✅ passes: `executeNextTx` only executes the queue entry at `txNonce`, and moves `txNonce` forward by one.<br>• DP-27 `executeNextTxRevertsDuringCooldown` ✅ passes: until `txCooldown` has passed since the entry at `txNonce` was queued, `executeNextTx` always reverts, whoever calls it and whatever it is given. With DP-25, no queue entry can be executed before its own cooldown has passed. This is the veto window.<br>• DP-26 `queuedTransactionExecutesAfterCooldown` ✅ passes: once the cooldown has passed, before the entry expires and with the PauseGuard not paused, anyone's `executeNextTx` executes it. So DP-27 is not vacuous, and the veto window ends when the cooldown does.<br>• `executeNextTx` compares against `txCooldown` as it is when `executeNextTx` runs, not as it was when the transaction was queued (`Delay.sol:208-211`). So the veto window lasts `txCooldown` only while `txCooldown` is held constant, as Proposition 2 holds it. `txExpiration` only limits how long after the cooldown a transaction can still be executed (`Delay.sol:212-218`), so it does not affect the veto window.<br><br>**FV — Once a veto moves `txNonce` past a transaction, that transaction can never be executed:**<br>• DP-29 `vetoedTransactionCannotExecute` ✅ passes: a module queues a transaction, the owner's `setTxNonce` moves `txNonce` past it, and `executeNextTx` with that transaction then reverts.<br>• DP-30 `entryPassedByTxNonceNeverExecutes` ✅ passes: from any state, once `txNonce` is past a queue entry, `executeNextTx` with that entry's transaction reverts, unless the same transaction has been queued again and sits at `txNonce`. Queuing it again makes a new entry, with its own veto window.<br>• DP-24 `txNonceNeverDecreases` ✅ passes: no write function moves `txNonce` backwards, so a vetoed entry stays vetoed, whatever later happens to `txCooldown` or `txExpiration`.<br><br>**On-chain — The veto window is 24 hours:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `txCooldown()` on the Delay Modifier must be 86,400 seconds (24 hours).<br><br>**FV — The Term multisig holders on the DelayOwnerSafe can veto Delay Modifier transactions within the 24-hour veto window, directly from the DelayOwnerSafe:**<br>• DV150L2-1 `approvedOwnersVetoThroughExecTransaction` ✅ passes. In one execution:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ An owner of the DelayOwnerSafe (a Term multisig holder, P2.6) approves a `setTxNonce(n)` transaction with `approveHash`, for an `n` the Delay Modifier accepts.<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ `execTransaction` runs it with that approval as the signature.<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ With the DelayOwnerSafe as the Delay Modifier's owner (P2.3), the call succeeds and sets the Delay Modifier's `txNonce` to `n`.<br>• DV150L2-1 sets the DelayOwnerSafe's threshold to 1. By SE150L2-6 (P2.4), with the real threshold of 5 (P2.6), five owners' approvals take the same path.<br>• DV150L2-1 assumes the DelayOwnerSafe owns the Delay Modifier (P2.3) and has no guard. The DelayOwnerSafe's guard is ConfigLockGuard (read below), which the next two bullets cover. The holders can veto at any point in the 24-hour veto window: by DP-32 (below), the owner's `setTxNonce` succeeds whatever the time.<br>• ConfigLockGuard lets the veto through. CL150L2-10 `checkTransactionAcceptsEverythingElse` ✅ passes: whatever `lockedDelay` is, the guard accepts every plain call that is not a locked call. The veto, `setTxNonce(n)` on the Delay Modifier, is a plain call. It is not one of the nine calls the guard locks on its locked modifier (CL150L2-6 to CL150L2-9, CL150L2-24). The guard's `checkAfterExecution` does nothing (`ConfigLockGuard.sol:141`), so DV150L2-1's path is unchanged.<br>• OD150L2-4 `guardedSafeCanStillVeto` ✅ passes. In this rule, ConfigLockGuard is installed on the DelayOwnerSafe with the Delay Modifier as its locked modifier, and the DelayOwnerSafe owns the Delay Modifier. An `execTransaction` to the Delay Modifier of `setTxNonce(n)` succeeds and `txNonce` becomes `n`, for an `n` the Delay Modifier accepts.<br>• OD150L2-4 stubs the signature check. By P2.4, `execTransaction` only acts once five Owners of DelayOwnerSafe, the Term multisig holders (P2.6), have approved (SE150L2-5, SE150L2-12), and their approvals pass it (SE150L2-6).<br>• DP-32 `ownerCanSetTxNonceAtAnyTime` ✅ passes: whatever the time, `txCooldown`, `txExpiration` and pause state, the Delay Modifier owner's `setTxNonce(n)` succeeds and sets `txNonce` to `n`, for any `n` the Delay Modifier accepts.<br><br>**On-chain — The setup formally verified above is deployed:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. The DelayOwnerSafe's guard slot (`0x4a204f620c8c5ccdca3fd54d003badd85ba500436a431f0cbda4f558c93c34c8`, `GuardManager.sol:66` in SafeL2 v1.5.0) must hold ConfigLockGuard. This is the same requirement as P4.DelayOwnerSafe.5.<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `lockedDelay()` on ConfigLockGuard must return the Delay Modifier.<br>• Assumes the DelayOwnerSafe runs SafeL2 v1.5.0, the version CL150L2, DV150L2-1 and OD150L2-4 check (`GuardManager.sol:66`). |

### Proposition 3 — Only the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe may pause, and only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe may unpause, the execution of Delay Modifier transactions, and if a pause outlasts the 24-hour expiration period following the cooldown, the Delay Modifier transaction can only be skipped or vetoed, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard constant for the PauseSafe and ProposerSafe, and 2. the guard, txCooldown, txExpiration constant for the Delay Modifier, and 3. the pauser and admin constant for the PauseGuard.

So a transaction whose window ended during the pause can be skipped during the pause.<br>• The Owner of Delay Modifier can also move `txNonce` past it with a veto, `setTxNonce` (P2.2).<br>• DP-30 `entryPassedByTxNonceNeverExecutes` ✅ passes: once `txNonce` is past the entry, `executeNextTx` with that entry's transaction reverts, unless the same transaction has been queued again and sits at `txNonce`. Queuing it again makes a new entry, with its own veto window.<br><br>**On-chain — The PauseGuard is the Delay Modifier's guard, and it is not paused:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `guard()` on the Delay Modifier must return the PauseGuard, as in P1.13.<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `paused()` on the PauseGuard must return false.<br><br>**On-chain — The Delay Modifier's expiration period is 24 hours:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `txExpiration()` on the Delay Modifier must be 86,400 seconds (24 hours), as in P1.13. |

### Proposition 4 — The owners for the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, and DelayOwnerSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, or DelayOwnerSafe. The fallbackHandler, modules, guard, module guard for the OwnerlessSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The following: 1. the fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the ProposerSafe and DelayOwnerSafe, and 2. the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown, txExpiration for the Delay Modifier cannot be changed by anyone.

### Proposition 5 — The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe. The pauser for the PauseGuard can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by anyone.

---

#### PauseSafe

##### P5.PauseSafe: The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe.

| # | Statement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P5.PauseSafe.1 | Only Modules of PauseSafe and Owners of PauseSafe can interact with the PauseSafe, except `execTransaction`, which anyone can call only if Owners of PauseSafe have approved the transaction, and except `fallback` and `receive`, which anyone can call but which do not change state, assuming the fallbackHandler is `address(0)`. | Same as P3.Pause.3. |
| P5.PauseSafe.2 | PauseSafe fallbackHandler is `address(0)`, which can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe and Modules of PauseSafe. | Same as P3.Pause.4.<br><br>**FV — PauseSafe fallbackHandler can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe or Modules of PauseSafe:**<br>• SC150L2-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set, the fallbackHandler only changes through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P5.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150L2-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once as many Owners of PauseSafe as the threshold have approved (SE150L2-5, SE150L2-12). So only Modules of PauseSafe or Owners of PauseSafe can change the fallbackHandler. |
| P5.PauseSafe.3 | `Modules of PauseSafe = null`, which can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`. | Same as P3.Pause.6.<br><br>**FV — Modules of PauseSafe can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`:**<br>• SC150L2-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set, the module list only changes through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P5.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150L2-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once as many Owners of PauseSafe as the threshold have approved (SE150L2-5, SE150L2-12).<br>• The PauseSafe has no module (P3.Pause.6), so only the Owners of PauseSafe can change the module list. |
| P5.PauseSafe.4 | `Owners of PauseSafe = Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe`, which can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`. | Same as P3.Pause.5.<br><br>**FV — Owners of PauseSafe can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`:**<br>• SC150L2-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set, the owners and threshold only change through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P5.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150L2-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once two Owners of PauseSafe, the Term multisig holders (P3.Pause.5), have approved (SE150L2-5, SE150L2-12).<br>• The PauseSafe has no module (P3.Pause.6), so only the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe can change the owners and threshold. |
| P5.PauseSafe.5 | PauseSafe guard is `address(0)`, which can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`. | **On-chain — PauseSafe guard is `address(0)`:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. The guard slot (`0x4a204f620c8c5ccdca3fd54d003badd85ba500436a431f0cbda4f558c93c34c8`, `GuardManager.sol:66` in SafeL2 v1.5.0) on the PauseSafe must hold `address(0)`.<br>• Assumes the PauseSafe runs SafeL2 v1.5.0, the version SE150L2 and SC150L2 check (`GuardManager.sol:66`).<br><br>**FV — PauseSafe guard can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`:**<br>• SC150L2-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set, the guard only changes through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P5.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150L2-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once as many Owners of PauseSafe as the threshold have approved (SE150L2-5, SE150L2-12).<br>• The PauseSafe has no module (P3.Pause.6), so only the Owners of PauseSafe can change the guard. |
| P5.PauseSafe.6 | The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe. | **FV — The Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe can change the owners, fallbackHandler, modules and guard for the PauseSafe through `execTransaction`:**<br>• SC150L2-3 `ownersCanChangeSettings` ✅ passes: for each of `addOwnerWithThreshold`, `removeOwner`, `swapOwner`, `changeThreshold`, `enableModule`, `disableModule`, `setGuard` and `setFallbackHandler`, an owner's (Owners of Safe) `execTransaction`, addressed to the Safe with a call to that function, succeeds and changes a setting once the threshold is passed.<br>• SE150L2-6 `ownersCanMakeTheSafeAct` ✅ passes: once the threshold is passed, `execTransaction` succeeds and the Safe acts, for any threshold and any number of owners. The PauseSafe runs SafeL2 v1.5.0 (P3.Pause.5), and its owners are the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe (P3.Pause.5).<br>• The PauseSafe has no guard (P5.PauseSafe.5), so nothing rejects the owners' `execTransaction`. |

---

#### PauseGuard

##### P5.PauseGuard: The pauser for the PauseGuard can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe; the admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by anyone.

| # | Statement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P5.PauseGuard.1 | Only the PauseGuard pauser and the PauseGuard admin can interact with the PauseGuard, except `checkTransaction` and `checkAfterExecution`, which anyone can call but which do not change state.                                                                                                     | Same as P3.1. |
| P5.PauseGuard.2 | `PauseGuard admin = ProposerSafe`, which cannot be changed by anyone.             | Same as P3.Admin.2.<br><br>**FV — Nobody can change the PauseGuard admin:**<br>• DP-14 `adminNeverChanges` ✅ passes: over every write function of the Delay Modifier and the PauseGuard, the admin never changes.<br>• `admin` is `immutable` (`PauseGuard.sol:17`), set once in the constructor, so no function can write it. |
| P5.PauseGuard.3 | `PauseGuard pauser = PauseSafe`, which can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. | Same as P3.Pause.2.<br><br>**FV — The PauseGuard pauser can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe:**<br>• DP-13 `pauserOnlyChangesThroughSetPauser` ✅ passes: over every write function of both contracts, the pauser only changes through `setPauser`.<br>• DP-10 `setPauserRevertsForAnyoneButTheAdmin` ✅ passes: anyone who is not the admin is rejected.<br>• The PauseGuard admin is the ProposerSafe (P5.PauseGuard.2), and only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can make it act (P4.ProposerSafe.1, P4.ProposerSafe.3, P4.ProposerSafe.4). So only they can change the pauser. |
| P5.PauseGuard.4 | The pauser for the PauseGuard can be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe; the admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe, so it cannot be changed by anyone.             | **FV — The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can change the PauseGuard pauser:**<br>• DP-11 `setPauserSetsThePauser` ✅ passes: for any nonzero account, the admin's `setPauser(account)` succeeds, `pauser()` then returns that account, and the previous pauser no longer holds the slot.<br>• SE130L2-6 / SE141L2-6 / SE150L2-6 `ownersCanMakeTheSafeAct` ✅ passes: once the threshold is passed, `execTransaction` succeeds and the Safe acts, for any threshold and any number of owners. So the ProposerSafe's owners (P3.Admin.5) can have it call `setPauser`.<br>• The ProposerSafe's guard is ConfigLockGuard (P4.ProposerSafe.5). Its call to `setPauser` on the PauseGuard is a plain call to neither the ProposerSafe nor its locked Delay Modifier, so it is not a locked call. CL130L2-10 / CL141L2-10 / CL150L2-10 `checkTransactionAcceptsEverythingElse` ✅ passes: whatever `lockedDelay` is, the guard accepts every plain call that is not a locked call. It checks ConfigLockGuard's `checkTransaction` directly, so the Safe version does not matter. Its `checkAfterExecution` does nothing (`ConfigLockGuard.sol:141`), so the call is unchanged.<br><br>**FV — The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe cannot change the PauseGuard admin, so nobody can:**<br>• Same as P5.PauseGuard.2: the admin never changes, whoever the caller is, the ProposerSafe included. |
